scope: Proposition 2.5 (Periodic-orbit matching) of the manuscript “Two limit cycles for quintic Liénard systems” (preprints/two-limit-cycles-for-quintic-lienard-systems-September-24-2026/two-limit-cycles-for-quintic-lienard-systems-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 33941e46486c5fef), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the system ẋ = y − F(x), ẏ = −x, (2.15) the images of nonconstant periodic solutions are in one-to-one correspondence with the zeros of ∆(r) = M+(0, r) − M−(0, r) (2.16) on the single open interval I = I+ ∩I−. If this interval is empty, there are no such periodic solutions. Each periodic orbit has exactly one positive and one negative intersection with the y-axis. Under the correspondence, isolated periodic orbits are exactly isolated zeros of ∆.
